This reads as a bond term-premium repricing that risk assets have so far absorbed, not a liquidity squeeze.

counterargs.read: Front-end and credit are calm and the dollar is soft — normally a green light for risk. But the long end is selling off and gold is surging, which looks more like a term-premium/fiscal-supply story than a growth or inflation scare. Equities have absorbed the back-up in yields so far, but rising real yields alongside surging gold is worth watching as a stagflation-adjacent tell rather than dismissing outright.
